active_paradigms.idea: Freeze the best discovered contact graph and refine its tangencies with scipy.optimize.root
active_paradigms.description: The current constructor is a many-start SLSQP search over all 78 center/radius variables, initialized almost entirely from five-row hexagonal layouts. Its strength is exact analytic inequality Jacobians and a final radius shrink certificate, which is why it reliably reaches about 2.63429. Its limiting weakness is that nearly all starts remain in the same local contact topology, while the repeated online SLSQP calls consume the runtime budget without preserving a single high-precision structural solution. Run the existing search offline once, retain its best candidate, identify its active wall contacts and near-tangent circle pairs, and embed that candidate plus this contact list as constants. At runtime, use scipy.optimize.root once on the square system formed by selected equations x-r=0, 1-x-r=0, y-r=0, 1-y-r=0, and distance(i,j)-r_i-r_j=0. Select an independent set of 78 equations, ideally chosen by QR pivoting of the existing analytic constraint Jacobian offline, so the root system is nonsingular. This yields a high-precision explicit packing in the same basin and can remove the loss caused by SLSQP termination and conservative feasibility scaling. Return the refined constants after applying only a tiny uniform radius factor such as 1-2e-9.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Increase the actual validated sum of radii by converting the incumbent’s approximate active-contact solution into a numerically sharp, explicitly reproducible packing; validity is mandatory because any overlap makes the score zero.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not infer the active graph afresh from a weak seed at runtime; freeze a graph from the best incumbent. Root does not enforce inactive inequalities, so verify every pair and every wall after refinement and reject/fall back to the frozen certified vector if an inactive constraint becomes violated. Use a safety factor smaller than the evaluator’s 1e-6 overlap tolerance margin, and ensure the returned arrays have exactly shapes (26,2) and (26,).

active_paradigms.idea: For a frozen high-quality center arrangement, obtain globally optimal radii by one scipy.optimize.linprog call
active_paradigms.description: At fixed centers, maximizing the sum of radii is not nonlinear: every containment limit is r_i less than or equal to min(x_i,y_i,1-x_i,1-y_i), and every non-overlap condition is r_i+r_j less than or equal to the fixed center distance. Thus the radius subproblem is an exact 26-variable linear program. The current code instead jointly optimizes positions and radii and then shrinks all radii by one common factor, so a single tiny bad contact reduces even circles that are not responsible for it. Embed a carefully selected center list from an offline high-scoring packing, build one A_ub matrix containing four boundary inequalities per circle and 325 pair inequalities, and call scipy.optimize.linprog with objective -ones(26), bounds r_i>=0, and method='highs'. The returned radii maximize the evaluator’s actual score for those centers, rather than using the unused compute_max_radii proportional-rescaling heuristic. This is especially useful after a contact-graph solution is rounded into source code, since linprog redistributes radius losses optimally instead of blindly scaling everything. The resulting output is deterministic and far faster than 168 SLSQP runs, allowing the constructor to be genuinely explicit.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly maximize np.sum(radii), which is exactly the evaluator’s sole non-binary objective, while retaining fixed centers known to have a favorable 26-circle topology.
active_paradigms.cautions: This cannot improve positions, so the embedded centers must come from a stronger offline candidate or a root-refined incumbent; do not use the original equal-hex seed. Distances in A_ub should be computed from the exact embedded float centers, then multiply linprog radii by about 1-1e-9 before returning to protect against serialization and feasibility tolerances. Include all 325 pairs, not only visually neighboring pairs, because the validator checks all pairs.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution once on a low-dimensional asymmetric contact-chart constructor
active_paradigms.description: The present search explores perturbations of only a few hexagonal row-count templates, so it is good at recovering the known hexagonal basin but weak at crossing contact-graph changes such as corner circles exchanging neighbors or unequal boundary layers. Replace the 78 unconstrained coordinates by a compact constructive chart: parameterize row heights, left/right boundary offsets, horizontal gaps, and a small number of independently varying boundary/interior radii, with remaining centers generated by cumulative gaps. Impose square containment and all pair separations through a large smooth violation penalty, while the feasible portion of the objective is negative sum of radii; parameter bounds should make generated points remain near a dense five-row packing. Call scipy.optimize.differential_evolution once with a fixed seed, Sobol initialization, workers=1, deferred updating, and a population/generation budget chosen to remain below 350 seconds. Unlike the current repeated local method, differential evolution can select different row staggering, uneven edge spacing, and deliberately broken mirror symmetry before local geometry becomes locked. After an offline run finds a topology exceeding the current result, freeze its chart parameters or centers into the final explicit constructor rather than repeating the global search for every evaluation. This targets a fundamentally different source of gain: escaping the current initialization family rather than merely tightening its numerical solve.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Discover a higher-sum unequal-radius topology, particularly boundary defect arrangements that cannot be reached from small perturbations of the 5-6-5-6-4 hexagonal seeds.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not run this in full 78-dimensional form; differential evolution will be ineffective there. The chart must enforce a fixed ordering of rows/columns to prevent label-swapping plateaus, and its penalty must be much larger than any possible radius-sum gain so infeasible candidates are never preferred. Since evaluator validity is all-or-nothing, certify and slightly shrink the final frozen solution; use the evolutionary call for offline discovery, not as the final expensive constructor.
